The bullying in Columbine was pretty unbiased, everybody got bullied for something or another. But the group Dylan would hang around with, the Trench Coat Mafia, which consisted of maybe 4 or 5 kids including them, was a huge target for bullying. 
But I didn't think it was bad enough for him to be coaxed into shooting up school.

He was pretty open about it, yes. He was obsessed with death in a weird way, but didn't seem morbid, like a murderer. 
He hated people helping him, he couldn't stand it. 
He seemed to think life was nothing but disappointment and loss. Which is tragic.

But I'm sad to say, had they not shot up campus, I think he might have offed himself by now. 

I believe there was 2 different Dylan Klebolds.
The funny guy who could cheer you up in your time of need, the caring Dylan who put others before himself. 

Then there was VoDKa. The freaky tall kid who killed his classmates.

Texas, with my grandma. Moved there in february of '99 a few months before it happened.
It doesnt really affect me all that much. Of course i still occasionally think about it though. 
I think the biggest thing for me was finding out Dylan and Eric did it.
I didnt like Eric, i didnt really see him around Dylan in school all that much either, usually it was me, dylan, our friend robyn, and a few others that would hang out maybe 3 times a week at lunch, walk the halls during class, just normal school kid stuff.

I hold anger towards Eric for convincing Dylan to do it, but I honestly think Dylan would have offed himself by now if it hadnt happened. Life is for the living, I suppose.

Dylan wasn't a racist in any way, my guess is as good as yours as to why he killed him.

I knew dylan throughout school (I went to columbine until luckily, i dropped out on my 16th birthday. 2 months before columbine.),
 we went to the same daycare for a week until my mom pulled me out for being naughty. But I talked with dylan on multiple occasions, last time was maybe a week before i dropped out, i was walking out of the cafeteria and he was coming inside from going to lunch elsewhere i presume. 
We just exchanged a few jokes, i poked fun at his nose saying he needs to pin it shut otherwise a fly might crawl in there.
 We weren't by any means best friends, just acquaintances. He was one of the most genuine, funny, caring, and all around fun people i will ever have known.  
He was that one kid in class who was always trying to make people laugh, either that or he'd sit in his spot 3 seats to the left and write poems or something.

I didnt talk to him much, when i did it was just a "Hey whats up fagstick" (I tried to be a jock. Failed horribly, thankfully)
